screening_rules.ELECTION: Official electoral or reviewed political evidence indicates a specific election, by-election, nomination, candidacy, voting or government-formation contest.
screening_rules.LEGISLATION: Reviewed or verified evidence identifies a bill, motion or parliamentary measure; registration still requires evidenced material resistance and sourced sides.
screening_rules.LEADERSHIP: Reviewed or verified evidence identifies an actual leadership ballot, challenge, vacancy contest or materially opposed leadership process.
screening_rules.CONFIDENCE_SUPPLY: Reviewed or verified evidence identifies an actual confidence, no-confidence, supply or government-survival contest.
screening_rules.BUDGET: Reviewed or verified evidence identifies a materially contested budget or appropriation passage process; routine budget publication alone is insufficient.
screening_rules.PROCEDURAL: Reviewed or verified evidence identifies a materially opposed parliamentary procedural objective with a verifiable result.
screening_rules.POLICY_ENACTMENT: Reviewed or verified evidence identifies an explicit implementation objective facing material political resistance and a verifiable decision outcome.
screening_rules.PUBLIC_PRESSURE: Reviewed or verified evidence identifies a defined public demand facing institutional resistance or inertia. Institutional self-reporting alone does not establish a public gain, concession or causal effect.

candidates.subject: Federal disallowance contest — Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative—Improved Forest Management in Multiple-use Public Native Forests) Methodology Determination 2026
candidates.evidence_summary: Official Parliament of Australia evidence records unresolved disallowance action against the 2026 native-forest carbon methodology determination. Senator Cadell's motion is postponed to 15 September 2026 and a separate House disallowance notice by Mr Tehan is also unresolved. This establishes a current procedural competition candidate within the 48th Parliament; opposing-side composition still requires resolution before match registration.

candidates.subject: AI Kill Switch and Data Centre Control Bill 2026
candidates.evidence_summary: Official Parliament of Australia evidence verifies that the AI Kill Switch and Data Centre Control Bill 2026 is currently before the House of Representatives after introduction on 7 September 2026. The bill is therefore a live legislative competition candidate; material resistance and both competition sides have not yet been evidenced sufficiently for registered-match promotion.
